title: Why is it raining inside my tent?
subtitle: The science of tent condensation

segments.narration: You wake up, and your tent is dripping. Did it rain overnight?
Not a single drop fell last night. So where did all this water come from? Let’s rewind.
Every breath you let out is warm and full of water vapor. Add what your skin gives off, and one sleeper puts about a cup of water into the air overnight.
Meanwhile, on a clear night, the fly is losing heat straight to the open sky. So it ends up colder than the air inside your tent.
When that moist air touches the cold fabric, it drops below its dew point, and the vapor turns back into liquid water. That’s your rain.
It’s worst on calm nights, in low spots near water, with every door zipped shut.
So give that vapor a way out. Open the vents, keep the fly tight, and pitch on higher, drier ground, under trees if you can.
It was never a leak. It was your breath. Follow CAMP LAB for more camping science.
